acip: GANG ZAG DE'I BLO YI MTHONG BA LA LTOS NA NI, MIG SHES DANG SKRA BSHAD {%SHAD} KYI RNAM PA STE SKRA SHAD DU SNANG BA'I YUL GNYIS CHAR YANG YOD PA YIN LA, DON GSAL MTHONG BA STE RAB RIB MED PA'I MIG GIS MTHONG BA LA LTOS NA NI SKRA SHAD DU SNANG BA DANG, DE SNANG BA'I SHES PA GNYIS KA'ANG BRDZUN PA STE MA SKYES PA YIN TE, SNANG BA TZAM GYI YUL YANG MED PAR SHES PA YOD PA NGES PAR DKA' BA'I PHYIR RO,,
english: Relative to what the mind of this person sees, the visual consciousness and the aspect of the strand of hair—the object which appears as though it were a strand of hair—do both indeed exist. Relative though to the sight of someone who is seeing objects clearly—that is, to the sight of an eye which has no cataracts—both the appearance of something as a strand of hair and the state of mind which holds this appearance are false; which is to say, neither one has actually grown. That is, it would be difficult to say that one ascertained the existence of a state of mind if there were not even any object which was just appearing to be there.
